summary: Modern databases have evolved far beyond storage and retrieval, embedding AI and ML capabilities directly into the data layer to eliminate costly data movement and enable real-time inference. By 2026, vector search has become a standard feature across virtually all major data platforms, with adoption growing 377% year over year as 75% of enterprise AI applications depend on vector search capabilities. The competitive frontier has shifted to LLM integration, automated embedding generation, and seamless orchestration with foundation models from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

databases.name: Snowflake
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI is a suite of fully managed AI functions built natively into the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. It provides text-to-SQL generation, automated embedding creation, sentiment analysis, summarization, and classification using foundation models without moving data outside Snowflake. Snowflake Postgres (generally available as of early 2026) runs natively in the platform with pgvector support, and Cortex AI integrates directly with it to provide embedding generation and text-to-SQL capabilities. Cortex Analyst allows business users to query data in natural language, while Cortex Search enables low-latency hybrid search over unstructured data.
databases.llm_integration: Supports multiple LLMs including Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and models accessible via Cortex AI functions such as COMPLETE(), EMBED_TEXT_768(), and EMBED_TEXT_1024(). Integrates with external models via external functions and supports bring-your-own-model patterns.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits. Embedding generation, LLM inference, and search are each metered separately per token or per query depending on the function. Snowflake Postgres is included within the AI Data Cloud but compute costs apply. Enterprise and Business Critical editions required for full governance features.

databases.name: Google BigQuery
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to build, train, and deploy ML models directly in BigQuery using standard SQL, supporting logistic regression, boosted trees, neural networks, matrix factorization, and time-series forecasting. The Vertex AI integration extends this with access to Google's foundation models, enabling text embedding generation, multimodal search, and LLM-powered SQL functions via the ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions. BigQuery Vector Search provides approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns stored natively in BigQuery tables, making it a unified store for both structured analytics and vector workloads.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI Model Garden, including Gemini models for text generation and embedding. ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.UNDERSTAND_TEXT functions expose PaLM 2 and Gemini capabilities directly in SQL. Supports remote models hosted on Vertex AI and external endpoints via BigQuery Connections.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML training costs are based on bytes processed. Vector Search queries are billed per query and by index size. LLM inference via ML.GENERATE_TEXT is billed through Vertex AI token pricing, which varies by model. BigQuery on-demand pricing is $6.25 per TB processed; flat-rate and capacity-based pricing available for high-volume workloads.

databases.name: PostgreSQL
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector data types and similarity search using L2 distance, inner product, and cosine distance. It supports exact and approximate nearest neighbor search via IVFFlat and HNSW indexing and is suitable for datasets up to approximately 50 million vectors without specialized infrastructure. pgai, developed by Timescale, extends Postgres further by adding functions to call embedding models and LLMs directly from SQL, enabling retrieval-augmented generation pipelines entirely within the database. This combination makes PostgreSQL the lowest-friction path to vector search for teams already running Postgres, with no new infrastructure required. Snowflake Postgres natively supports pgvector as of 2026.
databases.llm_integration: pgai enables direct calls to OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic, and Cohere embedding and completion APIs from within SQL functions. Vectorizer feature in pgai automates embedding creation and synchronization. Works with any Postgres-compatible platform including Supabase, Neon, AWS RDS, and Snowflake Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use. Infrastructure costs depend on hosting provider. Managed options include Supabase (free tier available, pro from $25/month), Neon (free tier available), AWS RDS for PostgreSQL (standard EC2 and storage pricing), and Timescale Cloud (from $0 on free tier). LLM API calls via pgai are billed by the respective model provider.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML integrates Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend, allowing ML inference to be called directly from SQL queries without exporting data. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector natively, enabling vector similarity search alongside transactional workloads. Redshift ML enables data teams to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL by automating model training on SageMaker AutoPilot and exposing predictions as SQL functions. Amazon Bedrock integration allows both services to call foundation models for embedding generation and text generation. Together these services cover both OLTP and OLAP AI use cases within the AWS ecosystem.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector for vector search and integrates with Amazon Bedrock for embedding generation using models like Amazon Titan Embeddings and Cohere Embed. Redshift ML integrates with SageMaker for custom model training and with Bedrock for generative AI inference. Both support external function calls to any API including third-party LLM providers.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference calls are billed per SageMaker inference endpoint hour plus data transfer costs. Redshift ML model training is billed via SageMaker AutoPilot pricing; predictions after deployment have no additional per-query cost beyond standard Redshift compute. Bedrock API calls are billed per token by model. Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector uses standard Aurora instance pricing starting around $0.073/hour for db.t3.medium.

databases.name: Databricks
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI and ML platform built on the Lakehouse architecture. MLflow is the open-source backbone for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment lifecycle management. DBRX is Databricks' own open-source foundation model optimized for enterprise workloads. Mosaic AI (formerly Databricks AI) unifies vector search, model serving, AI agents, and retrieval-augmented generation into a single platform. Databricks Vector Search provides a managed vector index over Delta Lake tables with automatic synchronization as underlying data changes, enabling always-fresh retrieval without manual re-indexing. The platform integrates with Hugging Face, LangChain, and LlamaIndex for building agentic AI systems.
databases.llm_integration: Supports serving DBRX, Llama, Mistral, and other open-source models via Mosaic AI Model Serving with GPU-backed endpoints. Integrates with external providers including OpenAI and Anthropic via AI Gateway for centralized routing, rate limiting, and cost tracking. MLflow tracks experiments and manages model versions across any framework including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face Transformers, and scikit-learn.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks pricing is based on Databricks Units (DBUs) which vary by workload type and cloud provider. Vector Search is billed per index hour and per query processed. Model Serving endpoints are billed per compute hour with GPU instances at premium rates. MLflow is open-source and free; managed MLflow on Databricks is included in workspace costs. Enterprise agreements typically required for production AI workloads at scale.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables semantic and hybrid search directly on data stored in Atlas clusters without requiring a separate vector database. It stores vector embeddings alongside operational documents in the same collection and builds HNSW indexes for approximate nearest neighbor search. Atlas Vector Search supports pre-filtering on any document field before vector search, enabling precise scoped retrieval for RAG applications. The feature integrates natively with popular AI frameworks and can be combined with Atlas Search (BM25-based text search) for hybrid retrieval that blends semantic and keyword relevance. As of 2026 it is listed among the top enterprise vector database solutions for teams already using MongoDB.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Hugging Face, and OpenAI via official connectors. Atlas integrates with major embedding providers including OpenAI, Cohere, and Voyage AI for automated embedding generation via Atlas Triggers or application-side pipelines. MongoDB AI Applications Program (MAAP) provides reference architectures combining Atlas with leading AI providers.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 dedicated clusters and above. Pricing is based on cluster tier, storage, and data transfer, starting at approximately $0.08/hour for M10 clusters. Vector index storage counts toward total storage allocation. Serverless Atlas instances do not currently support Vector Search indexes. Free tier (M0) does not support Vector Search.
